thread:
maria: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands: need a plain-language summary of the revamped release flow (cadence + who-does-what).
kevin: Summary: cadence = minor every 3 weeks, major = once a month. Minor releases are intended for incremental features/fixes; majors include schema/security bumps and require extra validation windows.
tara: Who is the primary owner for rollout decisions?
maria: Eng leads own the rollout plan. SRE/ops own the monitoring & rollback procedures. Product signs-off on user-impacting changes.
oncall-bot: Reminder: file a "canary runbook" in the release ticket and ping @oncall 24h before start.
ryan: Are feature flags still required for all UX changes?
kevin: Yes. Any customer-visible behaviour must be behind a flag or released as a controlled canary for >=24h.
docs: Can someone make a 1-pager checklist? I can publish it to the handbook.
tara: I'll draft the checklist (cadence, notif matrix, perf thresholds, runbook template). Need review from ops + eng leads.
ryan: Perf/quality gates 14 what's the measurable bar for p99/p95?
kevin: Gates: unit + integration green, staging smoke e2e green, perf: p99 <= 15% regression vs baseline and p95 <= 10%. Error rate absolute delta <= 0.5%.
sales-liaison: Customers are asking if SLAs change with this pace.
maria: No SLA changes to hosted. We will expose more per-route SLO metrics internally so sales can assess renewal risk.
docs: I'll add a small customer-facing blurb for AE use. Tag me when PRs land.
maria: Also proposing a short 15m post-release sync (optional unless rollback/alerts). Helps capture issues quickly.
kevin: Ops: please publish a calendar of blackout/maintenance windows so teams can avoid major ramps then.
oncall-bot: Note: when a canary crosses oncall shifts, confirm with incoming oncall 12h before.
tara: Thanks everyone 14 I'll open the PR to the handbook with the checklist + notif flow by Friday and drop the draft blurb for sales.
